name: smooth-scroll
title: Smooth Scroll
description: Smooth, interpolated scrolling for the page or a scroll container, built on Lenis: native scroll underneath, with a hook for the instance and scroll events.
label: Lenis
author: darkroom.engineering <https://github.com/darkroomengineering>

props.name: root
props.description: true smooths the page (the <html> scroller) and makes the instance global; false renders a wrapper and a content div that scroll on their own; "asChild" renders the wrapper but still makes the instance global.

props.name: options
props.description: Lenis options: lerp (0 to 1, default 0.1), duration, easing, wheelMultiplier, touchMultiplier, orientation, gestureOrientation, smoothWheel, syncTouch, infinite, autoRaf (default true), anchors, respectReducedMotion (default true)...

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the wrapper div (not rendered with root={true}). Give it a height and overflow-y: auto.

props.name: ref
props.description: { wrapper, content, lenis }: the two divs and the Lenis instance.

props.name: useSmoothScroll(callback?, deps?, priority?)
props.description: Returns the nearest Lenis instance (or the global one); the callback runs on every scroll. Same as the upstream useLenis, also exported.

a11y: Scrolling stays native: the keyboard (arrows, Page Up/Down, Space, Home, End), find in page, anchors and assistive technology scroll as usual; Lenis only interpolates wheel and programmatic scrolling.
Honours prefers-reduced-motion (Lenis's respectReducedMotion, on by default): wheel input tracks one to one and scrollTo jumps instead of animating.
In wrapper mode, give the wrapper tabIndex={0}, a role and a label (as the demo does) so keyboard users can focus and scroll it.
